profile.entities: Star Cement Limited; Silchar Grinding Unit; Siliguri Grinding Unit; Meghalaya Clinker Units
profile.subseg: OPC; PPC; Clinker Sales; AAC Blocks
profile.themes: Northeast Pricing Power; North India Greenfield Expansion; Subsidy Run-rate Normalization; Freight Cost Volatility

deepdive.sec: Cement / Regional Building Materials & Infrastructure Enablers

bull_bear.body: Priority on organic greenfield expansion in North and Bihar; Maintaining dividend discipline while leveraging balance sheet up to 1.5x limit before raising equity; No M&A mentioned.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body: 1) Regulatory: Crackdown on illegal coal mining in Meghalaya (management claims minimal impact due to FSA contracts); 2) Competition: New capacity by Dalmia/others in North India could pressure pricing; 3) Execution: Delays in environmental clearances for Rajasthan/Umrangso projects; 4) Subsidy: Structural lower run-rate due to GST changes until new units utilize input credits.
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: Confident on Northeast pricing power and volume growth; Cautious on North India entry emphasizing brand building over volume dumping; Transparent on subsidy headwinds and one-off freight costs; Aggressive on long-term capex vision.
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body: Silchar unit commissioning will initially absorb GST input credits for 7-8 months before becoming eligible for subsidies, delaying subsidy benefit to FY27; Jorhat grinding unit plan dropped in favor of Bihar to better utilize existing clinker; Rajasthan project eligible for 23% CAPEX capital subsidy from state government.
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

business.body: Cement Sales: 12.31 Lakh tons (+16% YoY); Clinker Sales: 0.65 Lakh tons; Northeast Volume: 9.36 Lakh tons; Outside Northeast: 2.95 Lakh tons; Blend: 82% PPC, 18% OPC; AAC Blocks: INR 13 Cr revenue (Q3), ramping to INR 90-100 Cr annual run-rate at full utilization (20% EBITDA margin target).
business.title: Segment / subsidiary detail

business.body:
| Challenge | Beneficiary/Loser | Dir | Conviction | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Aggressive capacity expansion in North India by incumbents and new entrants like Dalmia Bharat creating supply glut fears. | Dalmia Bharat Ltd | loser | Low | Star Cement's disciplined branding strategy may prevent price wars, but overall region profitability could compress affecting all players. |
| Freight cost volatility and coal supply disruptions in Northeast impacting regional players without captive logistics. | Star Cement Limited | beneficiary | Med | Star's ability to maintain INR 1,600/ton EBITDA despite freight spikes demonstrates operational resilience compared to peers. |
business.title: Challenges → beneficiaries & losers

latest_quarter.body: Realization up ~2% sequentially; Northeast prices up INR 20/ton YoY, East (Bihar/WB) neutral; Fuel cost stable at INR 1.2/kcal with 4-month inventory; Freight costs spiked due to one-off strike logistics but expected to normalize in Q4; Depreciation guidance: INR 90 Cr/quarter (stable until new plants commission).
latest_quarter.title: Margins & cost dynamics

outlook.body: Volume: ~5.3 Mn tons for FY26 (implies 10-12% growth in Q4); Margins: Expecting stability at INR 1,650-1,700/ton EBITDA; Capex: INR 150 Cr in Q4FY26, total INR 4,800 Cr over next 3-4 years for new projects; Commissioning: Silchar GU immediate; Rajasthan/Haryana plants by Sep FY28; Umrangso/Bihar by FY29.
outlook.title: Guidance

outlook.body: N/A (Commodity manufacturer); Demand visibility driven by 22% non-trade mix and 17.1% premium cement share in trade sales.
outlook.title: Order book & pipeline

outlook.body: 1) North India Entry: 3 Mn ton clinker (Nimbol, Rajasthan) + 2 Mn ton grinding (Haryana); 2) Bihar Expansion: 2 Mn ton grinding unit to utilize Northeast clinker; 3) Umrangso (Assam): New clinker plant to replace deferred Jorhat project; 4) Premiumization: Premium cement share increased from 12% to 17.1% YoY.
outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality

deepdive.thesis: Star Cement delivered a strong Q3FY26 with 21% volume growth and doubled EBITDA/ton to INR 1,600 driven by Northeast pricing power and premium mix shift, offsetting a 28% YoY drop in subsidy income. Management confirmed guidance of ~5.3M tons for FY26 and outlined a massive INR 4,800 crore capex plan for North India expansion (Rajasthan/Haryana) and Bihar, targeting commissioning from FY28-FY29 while maintaining a conservative leverage target (<1.5x Net Debt/EBITDA).
